A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KNG-based private geodesic-regression work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original sphere simulations, Wine Quality regression comparisons, and empirical sensitivity-bound checks in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original sphere, ADNI shape, and SPD(2) regression experiments, including budget, noise, and sensitivity-bound analyses in Section 4 and Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: Sequential KNG sampling is retained, but its sensitivity-based noise calibration changes substantially. V1's sphere bounds use cosine and sine Jacobi factors; v2 uses 2 tau/n for both parameters on nonnegatively curved manifolds and explicit hyperbolic-function bounds for negative curvature. These changes alter the sampling distributions, beyond merely explaining the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 removes the Wine Quality/Euclidean regression evaluation and adds synthetic SPD(2) regression and ADNI corpus-callosum shape regression. The latter uses 100 shapes represented by 50 landmarks and ages as predictors. Sphere evaluation remains, so coverage shifts substantially toward different manifold geometries and medical shape data.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates IBM Diffprivlib and Opacus against DPGR in Table 1 and Figure 4. That entire competitive comparison disappears; v2 compares its manifold results with nonprivate regression fits. Laplace, Gaussian, exponential-mechanism, and DP-SGD alternatives are discussed in Section 5 but are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sphere utility evaluation changes from MAE summaries to log-average MSE. V2 introduces equal-budget sweeps with total epsilon 0.2–2.0 and unequal allocations totaling 2.02, instead of the principal fixed 1+1 allocation. It also changes sample-size conditions and uses 10 footpoints with 10 vectors each per budget, replacing the earlier 200-replicate summaries.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic tests of budget imbalance and total budget, plus sphere data-spread experiments with noise levels 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1. The existing adjacent-dataset sensitivity validation expands from the sphere to SPD(2) and multiple dataset sizes. V1's separate footpoint-distance and shooting-angle diagnostics disappear.

E5.justification: V1 reports means, standard deviations, and utility error bars; v2's utility curves omit uncertainty intervals while sensitivity ratios are summarized with boxplots. The validation reports 100 adjacent-dataset pairs in v1 versus 20 pairs per size and manifold in v2. These revise replication and descriptive reporting without introducing significance testing or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V1's Wine Quality MSE entries—0.873 nonprivate, 0.954 DPGR, 7.856 Diffprivlib, and 0.982 Opacus—are removed, alongside its sphere MAE summaries. V2 supplies new log-MSE curves, shape and ellipse predictions, and sensitivity-ratio distributions. The new curves show higher errors at restrictive or extremely unequal budgets; changed metrics and settings prevent interpreting them as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the upper-curvature sensitivity argument with two-sided curvature assumptions and lower-curvature comparison bounds using operator norms and parallel/perpendicular Jacobi components. It adds gradient derivations and a geodesic-reach bound in Appendices B.3 and C, and rewrites Appendix D. However, Theorem D.1's negative-curvature formula differs from the proof's Equation 44 and main-text Equation 20.

C1.justification: The central claims of KNG-based private geodesic regression, Jacobi-field sensitivity, and general Riemannian applicability remain. V2 drops the separately advertised linear-regression contribution and benchmarking promise from the title and introduction. The additional manifold demonstrations principally support the retained central claim.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that the empirical residual bound used in both versions violates privacy and discusses how approximate MCMC sampling weakens pure-DP guarantees under mixing assumptions. It also explains instability under extreme budget allocations and cautions that similar-looking SPD ellipses need not be close geometrically. These materially qualify v1's more affirmative privacy and robustness interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies the nonprivate regression implementation as Regmi (2020) and discloses a 16 GB RAM laptop, Windows 11, and Jupyter environment. It documents ADNI landmark normalization and age scaling, plus SPD data generation and noise parameters. These are useful documentation additions, without establishing a solver change or providing a complete implementation release.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from comparison with established private-linear-regression tools to a manifold-regression setting claimed to lack existing DP alternatives. Section 5 develops substantive arguments about difficulties with output perturbation, exponential mechanisms, and DP-SGD. V2 also adds MCMC-privacy, shape-data, and SPD references while removing the Diffprivlib and Opacus references.

P1.justification: The sensitivity exposition, experimental narrative, and discussion are substantially rewritten. Common evaluation procedures move ahead of manifold-specific subsections, and the appendices are reorganized: geometry moves from C to B, sensitivity validation from B to G, and new derivation and analysis sections are integrated. The title and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. V1's comparison table and principal histograms are removed, while v2 introduces budget curves, shape predictions, noise-dependent sphere views, ellipse predictions, and sensitivity boxplots. The curvature schematic is retained and relocated from v1 Figure 7 to v2 Figure 4, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V2 materially strengthens the central sensitivity argument by correcting the curvature-comparison direction and accounting for both Jacobi components. Shape/SPD experiments and budget/noise analyses provide substantially better support for manifold applicability, while explicit privacy qualifications improve transparency. These gains outweigh the lost Euclidean comparisons and utility error bars. Important issues remain: the experimental tau is nonprivate, and Theorem D.1 conflicts with Equations 20 and 44.
